title: POC scoping: Apogee Systems - Redwood Integration Planning
summary: POC scoping focused on integration approach: SDKs vs OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling, structured output (JSON schemas), workload sizing, benchmarks (latency/cost targets), and a 6-week pilot timeline. Agreement to run initial bench on 50 concurrent RPS with a representative prompt set and to share security docs and pricing options.
topics: Workload sizing: RPS, tokens per request, KV cache impact
Benchmarks: latency p95, throughput, cost per 1k tokens
next_steps: Redwood to send POC proposal and pricing sheet (AE)
SE to share benchmark harness and sample scripts (Samira)
Customer to provide representative prompt set and sample payloads (Liu)
Security to share SOC2 + architecture doc link (Redwood)
Schedule on-prem/private deployment deep-dive if VPC required (week 2)
action_items: Alex Chen | Send POC proposal + pricing by 2026-03-06
Samira Patel | Share benchmark harness (Python + k6 scripts) by 2026-03-05
Liu Zhao | Upload representative prompt set and sample payloads by 2026-03-09
Priya Menon | List compliance questions / certs required by 2026-03-08
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. Quick rollcall?
[00:06] Ryan Cole (Apogee, CTO): Ryan here. Maya?
[00:08] Maya Singh (Apogee Eng Manager): Maya here.
[00:10] Liu Zhao (Apogee): Liu.
[00:11] Priya Menon (Apogee Security): Priya on the call.
[00:14] Alex: Great. Samira and Jordan from our SE team are also on.
[00:18] Samira Patel (Redwood SE): Hi everyone. Quick agenda: align on success criteria, confirm workload sizing and token profiles, pick integration approach (SDKs or OpenAI-compatible endpoint), discuss function/tool calling and structured output, and agree on bench plan and timeline.
[00:35] Ryan: Sounds good. At a high level, our goal for the POC is to validate latency at scale and make sure the structured outputs we rely on are high fidelity — we can't have downstream ETL break. Also security and data residency are must-haves.
[00:46] Maya: To add, we want to test a mix of short generation (single-turn 50-200 tokens) and long generation for summaries ~800 tokens. Our production traffic is spiky — about 50 RPS at peak, but bursts to 80-100 for short windows.
[01:12] Samira: Helpful. When you say 50 RPS, is that sustained or peak? And average tokens per request for the short gen?
[01:17] Maya: 50 sustained at peak hours, but average tokens for short gen is ~120 tokens. Long gen average 700-900 tokens but at lower RPS, more like 5-8 RPS.
[01:28] Jordan (Redwood): That maps to two workload classes. We'll size the bench: 50 sustained short-gen RPS with bursts to 100 for 2-3 minute windows, plus a background long-gen 8 RPS. Does that sound right?
[01:35] Ryan: Yes. Also want to validate KV cache benefits for our conversational use case — we have long session contexts.
[01:44] Samira: Noted. For cache we usually measure cold start vs warmed KV cache at various sequence lengths, because latency improvements are significant for warmed sessions. We'll include that in the bench harness.
[01:53] Priya: From security, we need to know data flows — where logs are stored, how customer data is retained, and KMS integration for keys. We prefer BYOK and want to confirm SAML SSO for the console.
[02:05] Alex: Yes, we'll include SOC 2 and encryption/KMS docs. We support KMS integrations (AWS KMS/GCP KMS), BYOK patterns, audit logs, and SAML for SSO. I'll send the security pack after the call.
[02:16] Ryan: On integration, we have a microservices architecture. We prefer an OpenAI-compatible endpoint so our engineers can reuse existing client libs, but we're open to using Redwood SDKs if there are benefits like batching and retries baked in.
[02:30] Samira: Good question. Our platform supports both: a drop-in OpenAI-compatible endpoint and Redwood SDKs (Python/Go/TS) that provide higher-level helpers — automatic batching, retry logic, streaming helpers, and easy function/tool calling wrappers.
[02:45] Maya: What's the delta in implementation effort? We have limited SRE cycles for the POC.
[02:49] Jordan: If you want the fastest path, OpenAI-compatible endpoint is usually quicker — same API semantics. But the SDKs reduce work on batching and integrated caching if you want to leverage them. For the POC we can start with the OpenAI-compatible endpoint and flip to the SDK for the performance runs if needed.
[03:05] Ryan: That sounds pragmatic. Also about function calling — we rely on deterministic JSON outputs for downstream processing. We need to ensure schema enforcement or at least high validity rates. How do you handle that?
[03:19] Samira: We can do a few things: (1) Use function/tool calling with a rigid JSON schema in the model call so the model is guided to return structured JSON. (2) Post-validate with a lightweight JSON schema validator in the client. (3) For production, we recommend a combination: function calling + schema enforcement + sampling-based monitors in Redwood Console to detect regressions. We'll calibrate temperature and prompt engineering during bench runs to hit the target validity.
[03:45] Priya: Any guardrails for tool calling — preventing exfiltration or unsafe system calls?
[03:50] Samira: Yes, we support allowlists for tool endpoints and sanitized input/output logging. For private deployments we can restrict network egress and enforce VPC-only tool endpoints. We'll share the security doc with the exact controls.
[04:05] Ryan: Good. Bench specifics — what metrics should we target? For us p95 latency under 300ms for short-gen is ideal, p95 under 1.2s for long-gen acceptable, and cost target below $X per 1k tokens (we'll be explicit in the POC sheet).
[04:28] Jordan: We'll design the bench to report p50/p90/p95, cold vs warm KV cache, throughput (RPS), error rates, and cost-per-1k tokens under the chosen model/quantization. We'll also produce token-level cost breakdowns in the results.
[04:44] Maya: About models, can you list the variants we can test? We need smaller low-latency models and higher-quality ones for summarization.
[04:52] Samira: We'll propose a matrix: quantized Llama-like variants for low latency, medium-sized open models (e.g., mix of community models), and a larger model for summaries. We'll provide verified performance profiles and recommend quantization knobs. If you want, we can include a Redwood-verified model that balances latency and quality.
[05:09] Ryan: For comparatives, we'd like an apples-to-apples comparison vs our current vendor (we mentioned Anthropic and OpenAI internally). Can you do a baseline run with OpenAI endpoints?
[05:20] Alex: We can run comparison tests — with your creds or using canonical prompts — typically we do synthetic bench plus a run on a dev dataset you provide. We'll note differences in API semantics if you use the OpenAI endpoint.
[05:31] Liu: Tech question: Do your OpenAI-compatible endpoints support function calling param schemas the same way as OpenAI's?
[05:38] Samira: Yes, function calling is supported in our compatibility layer. There are occasional differences in field names in generated traces due to transcription, but functionally we map the parameters so your existing clients should work. We'll include a sample curl and Python example.
[05:52] Ryan: Great. Timeline — we're aiming to have a decision and baseline results within 6 weeks. Proposed milestones?
[05:58] Jordan: Week 0 (this week): align and get prompt sets + security questions. Week 1: POC environment setup (hosted or dedicated nodes), bench harness prep. Week 2-3: run bench iterations and adjust prompts/temperature. Week 4: deep QA on structured output + function calling. Week 5: final performance run and cost analysis. Week 6: deliverables and go/no-go. We'll be flexible but that's the default plan.
[06:25] Maya: That fits our timeline. On deployment mode, we might require a VPC private deployment due to regulations depending on the PII handling.
[06:34] Priya: Correct, data residency and PII controls are gating. We'll need a quick architecture review for VPC options.
[06:40] Alex: If VPC is required, we'll do a short private deployment deep-dive in week 2. For the POC itself we can start on hosted with strict retention and KMS while we evaluate VPC.
[06:49] Ryan: About observability — we need per-route latency, per-token cost, and per-session traces.
[06:55] Samira: Redwood Console provides token-level costing, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. We'll show an example dashboard during the demo and attach exportable CSVs for your SRE.
[07:06] Liu: One more on schema: sometimes the model returns extra fields or slightly malformed JSON. Can you enforce strict schema rejection so we can catch those in the pipeline?
[07:17] Samira: We can. The model-call layer can be configured to accept only exact schema matches; we can force a failure or a sanitized fallback if the output doesn't validate. In the POC we'll test several enforcement modes to find the best tradeoff between strictness and throughput.
[07:33] Ryan: OK. Anything else?
[07:35] Alex: Quick note on SDKs: our Python SDK includes streaming helpers and a structured-output validator. I'll include sample repo links. The OpenAI-compatible endpoint will be easiest to bolt in, then we can swap to SDK for the high-performance run.
[07:48] Maya: For benchmarks, please include cost extrapolation to monthly usage — helps our finance folks.
[07:54] Jordan: Will do. We'll include cost modeling and sensitivity to batching and caching settings.
[08:02] Priya: From security, please confirm retention windows and ability to purge logs per request.
[08:09] Alex: Yes, retention controls and purge APIs exist; we'll detail that in the security pack.
[08:15] Ryan: Let's capture decisions: start with OpenAI-compatible endpoint for initial integration; run bench at 50 sustained RPS with 100 RPS bursts; include KV cache cold vs warm; test function calling with strict schema mode; share security docs; and target a 6-week POC with the milestones Jordan laid out.
[08:33] All: Agreed.
[08:36] Alex: I'll follow up with the POC proposal and pricing, Samira will share the harness, and Liu will upload prompts.
[08:42] Ryan: Thanks everyone.
[08:44] Maya: Thanks.
[08:46] Priya: Thanks.
[08:48] Samira: One small caveat — transcription note: some of the technical terms might be auto-transcribed oddly (k-v cash vs KV cache), so we'll annotate docs.
[08:57] Alex: Good call. We'll put the exact CLI and curl examples in the repo link.
[09:04] Jordan: Expect the benchmark scripts in a GitHub gist; will include instructions for OpenAI-compatible mode and SDK mode.
[09:12] Ryan: Perfect. End of call.

Notes: Some filler/overlap in speakers; occasional auto-transcription errors (e.g., 'k-v cash' for KV cache, 'redwood' sometimes lowercase), kept to preserve realistic Fireflies export feel. Links referenced: POC proposal doc (link: https://redwood.ai/poc/apogee-proposal), benchmark gist (link: https://gist.github.com/redwood/apogee-bench), security pack (internal link will be shared via email).
